root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting off or removing.
root_idea.development: The recorded semantic range develops from cutting to vegetation being cut off or consumed, barren land, destruction, sharpness, voracious eating, dearth, emaciation, infertility, and a cough that cuts the throat.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested adjective is displayed under its normalized citation-form headword جُرُزٌ rather than either inflected occurrence.

senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, it qualifies land or a surface made bare of vegetation. The reported explanations include vegetation cut off from its roots, consumed, or absent because of drying or lack of rain; these describe the same barren-land sense rather than separate meanings.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the destruction or killing of a person or thing, including complete extirpation.
A separate Form I verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat much or voraciously, leaving nothing on the table; also, to eat quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is verbal and describes a great or rapid eater.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey through barren land; consequently, to suffer or become afflicted by dearth, scarcity, drought, or barrenness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people in the construction أَجْرَزَ القَوْمُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to become lean or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use specifically attested with a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year of dearth, scarcity, drought, sterility, or barrenness.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for complete removal or destruction, including the proverbial expression لَنْ تَرْضَى شَانِئَةٌ إِلَّا بِجَرْزَةٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bundle or handful of qَتّ or similar herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for a gathered bundle or handful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cutting with a sword; a sword-cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for the act or result of cutting by sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cutting or penetrating sword; one that cuts sharply or cuts off utterly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a sword, including one characterized by exceptional sharpness or complete severing power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A devourer and breaker of trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application to a she-camel, likening its eating to the action of a cutting sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A voracious eater who leaves nothing behind; by extension, a voracious eating animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals, including a man, woman, camel, or she-camel; rapid eating may also be included.
Applied primarily to land and figuratively to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry and rugged land enclosed by sand or by a level tract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is especially associated with such land in or around sea islands.
A figurative extension of the root’s cutting notion, used of the intensity of the cough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, hard, or solid; also said of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Classical expression understood as transferred from the rough, hard character of barren land.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Cutting is represented directly; the land-with-vegetation-cut-off clause is covered by the Quranic barren-land sense.
Killing is included in the destruction branch.
Journeying in barren land and suffering dearth.
A year of dearth or drought.
Barren land lacking or deprived of vegetation.
A bundle or handful of herbage.
Figurative application to a tree-eating she-camel.
A voracious eater applied to people or animals.
Barren land and figuratively an infertile woman.
Dry, rugged land enclosed by sand or a level tract.

cautions: The Quranic lexical sense is barren or vegetation-deprived land. The lexical discussion records differing explanatory causes, including lack of rain, drying, and vegetation consumed; it also reports a divergent interpretation involving land that retains much water. These are treated as interpretive variants, not additional Quranic senses.
